newsitem.title: UK: BOXING-BENN RETIRES AGAIN AFTER DEFEAT BY COLLINS.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-BENN RETIRES AGAIN AFTER DEFEAT BY COLLINS.

text.p: Briton Nigel Benn threw his gloves into the crowd to signal his retirement from boxing after losing to Irishman Steve Collins on Saturday.

The 32-year-old, who had been cheered into the ring by the majority of a sell-out 22,000 crowd had to endure a storm of booing following the decision to pull him out of the fight at the end of the sixth round.
Chants of "what a lot of rubbish" came from sections of the arena as Collins retained the World Boxing Organisation (WBO) super-middleweight title.
Benn tried vainly to address the crowd using the ringside microphone , but had difficulty making himself heard before he said: "I tried to do everything for the public.
"I tried to go out pleasing the public but I can't do it anymore. I can't go on. I am calling it a day."
Benn twice changed his mind about quitting after losing to Collins in their first fight in July and surrendering his World Boxing Council (WBC) title to South African Thulane Malinga in March.
Collins appealed to the crowd to stop booing saying: "Please give him a hand. He's a great warrior, one of the greatest boxers of our time."
